I need to write thorough JUnit 4 tests for the Document class, so I'm mapping out each method's branches—constructor, createShell's null validation, head/body accessors, title's two paths depending on whether titleEl exists, title setter's validation and branching logic, createElement, and normalise's multiple conditionals.

I'm also covering the private helper methods indirectly through normalise(): the text node normalization loop that checks for blank nodes and moves them, the structure normalization that handles duplicate elements and reparenting, and the recursive tag-name search used by head()/body(). Beyond that I need tests for outerHtml, the overridden text() and nodeName(), clone(), and the OutputSettings inner class covering escapeMode, charset (in its various overloads), prettyPrint, and indentAmount with its validation check.

I'm deciding to place the test class in the same org.jsoup.nodes package so I can reach package-private methods like encoder() without extra imports, while still verifying that outputSettings(OutputSettings) throws on null via Validate.notNull, and adding coverage for the QuirksMode enum and its getter/setter.

I also need to confirm Validate.notNull and Validate.isTrue likely throw IllegalArgumentException when checks fail, so I'll design my tests to expect that exception type. Now I'm sketching out test methods, starting with one that verifies a null base URI throws the expected exception.

Then I'll continue covering shell creation with a valid base URI, head() behavior both with and without an existing head element, body() behavior similarly, title() returning empty or actual text, the title setter's null check and its behavior adding or updating a title element, element creation, and finally normalise() ensuring html/head/body structure gets created when missing.

Next I plan tests for normalise() moving stray text nodes into body and merging duplicate head/body elements, plus outerHtml, text setter, node name, and clone behavior. Then I want to cover OutputSettings thoroughly: default values, escape mode, charset getter/setter via both Charset object and String, pretty-print and indent amount settings (including the negative-indent exception), cloning settings, and how Document's outputSettings setter rejects null and otherwise applies correctly.

I also need quirks mode tests—confirming the default is no-quirks and that the setter/getter works as expected. Since Document, Element, Node, TextNode, and Tag are jsoup source classes compiled alongside the tests in this project (not external jar dependencies), I can reference them directly, using Document.createShell(baseUri) as the starting point for structural normalise tests.

For checking that normalise moves misplaced content, I'm planning cases where a Document is built without the standard html/head/body shell, or where a TextNode gets appended directly to the document outside head/body, then verifying normalise() reorganizes things correctly—like merging duplicate head/body elements or relocating stray text into the body. I also need to confirm how Element exposes its childNodes list and methods like appendElement, prependElement, and appendChild so the tests can construct these scenarios properly.

Then I'll grab the html element, append a duplicate head element directly onto it to bypass normal structure, and add a child like a meta tag inside that extra head to test duplicate handling.

I'm sketching a test that creates a shell document, appends a duplicate head element with a meta tag to it, verifies there are two heads before normalizing, then checks that after calling normalise() there's only one head and the meta content got merged into it. I'd write a similar test for duplicate body elements with an extra paragraph to confirm content gets consolidated under the single html parent.

Still writing shell setup...

I should write a similar test for body getting reparented when it's a sibling rather than child of html, and also think about testing the case where multiple head/body elements exist before normalise() runs its merge logic.

Looking at findFirstElementByTagName's recursion, I want a test case where the head element is nested deeper under an extra wrapper div, to confirm the recursive search actually traverses beyond immediate children rather than just checking the first level.

I also want to test that head() and body() safely return null when a document has no children at all—the loop never executes and null is returned directly, hitting that branch cleanly. Similarly, for title(), I should check that when no title element exists, the method returns an empty string.

For the setter title(String), I need cases for a null argument throwing IllegalArgumentException, creating a new title element under head when none exists, and updating an existing title element otherwise—plus verifying that title() trims whitespace from the stored text even though the setter itself doesn't trim on write. Then for createElement(tagName), I want to confirm the new element inherits the document's base URI.

I also need to check outerHtml() returns the full document markup including the html tag, text(String) only updates the body's text while leaving head/html structure intact, nodeName() returns "#document", and clone() produces a deep copy with its own OutputSettings instance holding equal but separate values (including charset). For OutputSettings itself, I should verify the defaults—base escape mode, UTF-8 charset, pretty print true, indent amount 1—and that setters like escapeMode return the same instance for chaining.

Now I'm working through charset setters: setting a Charset or charset name like "ISO-8859-1" should update charset() and the underlying encoder accordingly, prettyPrint(false) and indentAmount(int) should update their respective getters, with negative indentAmount throwing IllegalArgumentException, and clone() should produce an independent copy unaffected by later changes to the original.
